Generic.Label: Generic d20 (configured paths)
Generic.MenuHint: For game systems without a FastFighting helper module: where to find HP, AC, attack bonus and damage on actors.
Generic.Hint: Property paths on the actor, e.g. system.attributes.hp.value. Leave attack or damage empty to estimate them from level.

runs.Name: Simulations per estimate
runs.Hint: How many battles to simulate. More is steadier but slower; 2000 takes well under a second for a typical fight.

maxRounds.Name: Maximum rounds
maxRounds.Hint: A simulated battle still going after this many rounds counts as a stalemate.

includeHidden.Name: Include hidden tokens
includeHidden.Hint: Hidden tokens (ambushers, reinforcements) take part in estimates by default.

includeOtherLevels.Name: Include other scene levels
includeOtherLevels.Hint: Include tokens on scene Levels other than the one being viewed.

neutralDefault.Name: Neutral tokens
neutralDefault.Hint: Default handling of tokens with Neutral disposition. Can be changed per battle and per token.

secretDefault.Name: Secret tokens
secretDefault.Hint: Default handling of tokens with Secret disposition.

downedModel.Name: Downed characters
downedModel.Hint: How falling to 0 HP is simulated. 'Simulate dying and healing' follows the system's rules for dying, recovery and revival.

pcHealAggro.Name: Default PC healing
pcHealAggro.Hint: How freely player characters spend spells, potions and actions on healing, unless set per character in the Battle Planner.

pcAllyDying.Name: Default PC response to a dying ally
pcAllyDying.Hint: What player characters prioritize when an ally is dying, unless set per character.

leadership.Name: Leadership
leadership.Hint: Leaders (best social or warfare skill, Commanders, rallying abilities) raise their side's bravery and coordination while standing.

morale.Name: Morale and routing
morale.Hint: Combatants may waver or flee based on bravery, wounds, losses and a fallen leader or master.

positioning.Name: Positioning and terrain
positioning.Hint: Use token distances, movement types, terrain costs, walls and elevation. Turn off for theater-of-the-mind scenes.

surpriseDefault.Name: Initiative
surpriseDefault.Hint: Use the combat tracker's initiative when present, roll Stealth for hidden or Secret tokens, or roll normally.

lootMode.Name: Make it So: loot
lootMode.Hint: What happens to a slain creature's gear: leave it on the corpse (lootable), drop it in a loot pile, or do nothing.

corpseMode.Name: Make it So: corpses
corpseMode.Hint: Keep slain tokens on the map with the dead marker, or remove them (when a loot pile is dropped).

fledMode.Name: Make it So: fled combatants
fledMode.Hint: Hide tokens that fled the battle, or leave them where they are.

sideDefaults.Name: Side personality defaults
sideDefaults.Label: Configure
sideDefaults.Hint: Default group Tactical, Brave, Selfish and Loyal values for Friendly, Hostile, Neutral and Secret sides.

talking.Name: Talking
talking.Hint: Characters may try to de-escalate: talk enemies who share a language into surrendering, fleeing, or (rarely, unless neutral) switching sides.

storyStyle.Name: Story style
storyStyle.Hint: How the story of a fight is told in the Sample fight tab and in chat after Make it So: Roleplay (prose), Standard (what everyone did) or Statistician (every roll).

storyMode.Name: Story delivery
storyMode.Hint: Post the story publicly, or whisper it to GMs only.

bystanders.Name: Bystanders can join
bystanders.Hint: Tokens on the map that are not in the encounter may notice the fight (by sight or sound, muffled by walls), be called for help, be hunted, or be run into by someone fleeing, and then decide whether to join.

genericFallback.Name: Use the experimental generic adapter
genericFallback.Hint: Only for systems without a FastFighting helper module: guess HP, AC, attacks and damage from configured data paths. Expect rough results.

aftermath.Name: After the fight
aftermath.Hint: When the last enemy falls: the survivors tend their dying (first aid, healing feats, spells and potions) and anyone left untended lives or dies by the system's rules for dying, and the story tells it; or the same happens but the story ends at the last blow; or everyone is left exactly as the fight left them, for you to play out.

opening.Name: How encounters open
opening.Hint: Talk if they'd rather: the encounter opens as a standoff when every side's leader (or most of a leaderless side) would rather talk, or when almost everyone would. Nobody fights until someone gets upset: an insult, failed pitches piling up, a beast that can't follow the talk, or an impatient temper. Always talk first: every encounter opens that way. Straight to battle: no standoff.

concedeLuck.Name: PC luck: handing over an item
concedeLuck.Hint: When a player character is talked into giving up an item, they lose it only if a hidden d100 comes up at or under this. Higher means PCs lose items more often.

theftLuck.Name: PC luck: being robbed
theftLuck.Hint: A thief who beats a player character's defenses still needs a hidden d100 at or under this to take anything. Higher means thieves succeed more often.

playOnMap.Name: Make it So: play the fight on the map
playOnMap.Hint: The tokens run through the fight as the story tells it, quickly and around walls, before settling where the fight left them. Off: they go straight to where they end up.

Defaults.Hint: Group personality for each side. Every member's own values are blended with these, and both can be fudged per battle.

Planner.Title: Battle Planner
Planner.PositioningHint: Distances, movement types, terrain cost, walls and elevation
Planner.RefreshHint: Re-read the tokens on the scene
Planner.Disposition: Tactics (ask your player, or use Prepare Players)
Planner.NoAdapter: FastFighting has no support for this game system yet. A helper module can add it.
Planner.TalkingHint: Let characters talk foes down by persuading, threatening or bluffing them
Planner.BystandersHint: Tokens not in the encounter may notice the fight and join it
Planner.SceneChanged: You're viewing a different scene now. Run the battle again for this scene.
Planner.ThroughWall: no way round: through a wall

Results.Stale: Settings changed since this run. Run again to update.
Results.EmptyBody: Every token on the scene is listed on the left by side. Adjust personalities, allegiances and dispositions, then run thousands of simulated fights.

Swing.Hint: Re-runs the battle without each combatant and modifier to show what moves the party's odds most.

Sample.NotFound: No simulated fight matched that outcome. It may be very unlikely.

MakeItSo.Title: Make it So
MakeItSo.Confirm: Commit this fight's outcome to the tokens? The following changes will be made:
MakeItSo.UndoHint: You can undo this from the Sample fight tab.
MakeItSo.Failed: Make it So could not update {name}. See the console for details.
MakeItSo.Done: The outcome has been committed to the tokens.
MakeItSo.UndoConfirm: Restore the tokens to how they were before the last Make it So on this scene?
MakeItSo.SurrenderedHint: Laid down arms during a FastFighting battle and is at the victors' mercy.
MakeItSo.Hint: Post this story to chat, move every token to where the fight left it, and commit the outcome. Undo reverses all of it.
MakeItSo.Kept: Agreed to give up {what}, but kept it (luck {luck})
MakeItSo.Reclaimed: Gave up {what} to {name}, but got it back when {name} was beaten
MakeItSo.Doors: Doors: {n} opened ({broken} of them broken or forced)

preferredAction.Label: Favorite weapon or attack
preferredAction.Hint: The attack this character reaches for first. They still switch when something else is clearly better.

style.Label: Fighting style
style.Hint: How this character likes to fight.
style.frontline: Front line: close in and hold the line
style.skirmisher: Skirmisher: flank, strike twice, keep moving
style.ranged: Ranged: keep my distance and shoot
style.protector: Protector: guard my allies, shield up

target.Label: Who to attack first
target.Hint: Target priority when there is a choice.

resourceUse.Label: Spell slots, focus and limited abilities
resourceUse.Hint: How readily this character spends resources that only come back after rest.
resourceUse.balanced: Use them when they are clearly better
resourceUse.nova: Spend freely to end it fast

healAggro.Label: Healing others
healAggro.Hint: How freely this character spends actions and resources healing allies.
healAggro.conservative: Only when someone is dying or badly hurt
healAggro.allCosts: Heal at all costs, even with my last resources

potionThreshold.25: Below a quarter of my HP
potionThreshold.Label: Drinking my own potions
potionThreshold.Hint: When this character drinks healing potions or elixirs.

allyDying.Label: When an ally is dying
allyDying.Hint: What this character does the moment a friend goes down.

selfRevived.Label: After I'm revived
selfRevived.Hint: What this character does after getting back up.

retreat.Label: When to retreat
retreat.Hint: When this character would leave the battle.
retreat.losing: When the battle turns against us

shield.Label: Shield
shield.Hint: How this character uses Raise a Shield.

notes.Label: Anything else the GM should know
notes.Hint: For example: protect Ezren at all costs; won't harm the dog.

talk.Label: Talking instead of fighting
talk.Hint: Whether this character tries to end fights with words: persuading, threatening or bluffing foes who share a language into surrendering, fleeing or switching sides. It takes several successes to convince most foes, and anyone this character has hurt or failed to convince is much harder to sway.
talk.first: Talk first: try to end it with words
talk.never: Let my weapons do the talking

beyond.Label: Others nearby
beyond.Hint: Creatures on the map who aren't in the encounter yet. Run to fetch your allies when the fight goes badly, or hunt down enemies still about once the fight is won.
beyond.seekHelp: Run for help when it goes badly

Survey.Title: Prepare for Battle
Survey.Intro: Your GM wants to know how your characters fight in {scene}. Answers save as you go, and anyone sharing a character sees changes live.
Survey.NoTokens: You don't control any tokens on this battle map.
Survey.ResetHint: Return every answer for this character to "let them decide".
Survey.AutoHint: "Let … decide" is what your character would probably do. Change anything you'd do differently.
Survey.Thanks: Thanks! Your GM can see you're ready.
Survey.PrepareHint: Open a tactics survey on every player's screen for the tokens they control on this map.
Survey.NoPlayers: No players control tokens on this scene.
Survey.NoPlayersHere: No players control tokens on this scene. Fill in tactics yourself in each PC's row.
Survey.WillOpen: {name} is offline; their survey will open when they log in.

Playstyle.Label: Playstyles
Playstyle.Hint: Pick up to four labels that describe how this character really plays, in order of importance: the number on each pill is its place. Every pill counts, the first in full and each later one less (75%, 55%, 40%): in personality, quirks, desires, and tactics (where pills disagree, each simulated fight goes with one of them, the first most often). Unpick one and the later ones move up. They change what "Let them decide" means, how the simulation predicts the character, and how it picks up desires.
Playstyle.Max: Pick at most four playstyles. Unpick one first.
Playstyle.StayTrue: Stay mostly true to my calculated tactical level
Playstyle.StayTrueHint: Your answers and playstyles can only move the calculated strategy by about 10%: trait shifts are capped at ±10, and any choice that differs from the calculation shows up in only about 1 in 10 simulated fights.
Playstyle.Roleplay: Roleplaying is very important to me
Playstyle.RoleplayHint: The simulation weighs your playstyles heavily: their personality shifts double and their quirks (finishing foes, parleying, studying enemies…) happen much more often.
Playstyle.Both: Both boxes are checked: roleplay strengthens your playstyles, but staying true still caps how far they move you from the calculated strategy.

scaredyCat.Name: Scaredy-Cat
scaredyCat.Hint: Much less brave: hangs back, drinks potions early, retreats when hurt, goes unnoticed. Wants above all to keep away from the most dangerous foe, gives up easily, and hits back half-heartedly.

cruel.Name: Cruel
cruel.Hint: Picks on the weakest and finishes off the fallen; hits back hard, and enjoys leaving a foe hampered.

moralist.Name: Moralist
moralist.Hint: Never strikes a fallen foe; wants to heal friends and guard the weakest of them.

peoplePleaser.Name: People-Pleaser
peoplePleaser.Hint: Goes along with the group: wants what its leader and friends want (and listens to them far more than most), heals generously, protects friends, likes to talk, and is happy to bolster a friend.

fragile.Name: Fragile
fragile.Hint: Less brave; drinks potions early, retreats when hurt. Once hurt, wants to get away from whoever is hurting it and to mend itself; setbacks wear it down.

impatient.Name: Impatient
impatient.Hint: Charges the nearest foe, spends resources freely, skips the shield. A short fuse: setbacks wear it down twice as fast, and it has little patience for a locked door.

brawler.Name: Brawler
brawler.Hint: Loves melee: front line, the nearest foe, braver, hits back hard, no talking.

skeptic.Name: Skeptic
skeptic.Hint: Careful and calculating: saves resources, heals sparingly. Trusts its own judgment: its leader and team sway it half as much, and it's slow to talk.

speedRunner.Name: Speed-Runner
speedRunner.Hint: Wants it over fast: spends everything, goes for the quickest kills.

leader.Name: Leader
leader.Hint: Steps up to lead the side, braver and more loyal, goes for the biggest threat (and now and then pins it down), looks after its people and bolsters them. When it isn't the side's leader, it mostly goes its own way.

instigator.Name: Instigator
instigator.Hint: Acts first and spoils everyone else's plans: would rather lock a foe down, harass it or weaken it (trips, frights, hexes, holds) than simply hit it, more than any other playstyle. Picks fights with the most dangerous foe and the other side's leader, draws attacks, and may defy its own leader.

diplomat.Name: Diplomat
diplomat.Hint: Opens by trying to talk, wants to talk throughout, and often spares the fallen.

wallflower.Name: Wallflower
wallflower.Hint: Stays at range and out of notice; keeps its distance from whatever comes close, would rather hamper a foe from afar, and listens to the crowd less.

martyr.Name: Martyr
martyr.Hint: Never retreats, heals at all costs, and wants above all to guard the weakest friend; fears nothing; avenges the fallen twice as hard.

mercenary.Name: Mercenary
mercenary.Hint: Looks out for number one: easy pickings, conserves resources, keeps fighting over rescuing, retreats when it turns. Little loyalty: barely avenges anyone, gives up when it gets hard.

enabler.Name: Enabler
enabler.Hint: Support first: wants to heal, guard and bolster friends, and backs the leader.

redeemSeeker.Name: Redeem-Seeker
redeemSeeker.Hint: Out to prove itself: takes on the biggest threat, fights on the front line to save others, never retreats, and won't give up.

loreCollector.Name: Lore-Collector
loreCollector.Hint: Studies a new foe before fighting it (Recall Knowledge), then fights it better; drawn to foes it hasn't sized up yet.

puzzleManiac.Name: Puzzle-Maniac
puzzleManiac.Hint: Much more tactical: exploits weaknesses, goes after casters, likes a clever lock-down, and loves a locked door (keeps at it twice as long).

wildcard.Name: Wildcard
wildcard.Hint: Unpredictable: some foe catches its eye at random, nobody's voice counts for much, and it may defy its leader.

Playstyle.AlwaysTalk: This character always prefers talking to fighting
Playstyle.AlwaysTalkHint: Talks whenever there's someone to talk to, whole turns at a time, even without much skill at it, and always votes to open an encounter as a standoff. With "stay mostly true" also checked, it only makes talking a little more likely.

thief.Name: Thief
thief.Hint: Light fingers: when their side is winning, or they're unseen and someone is alone, they may rob a foe within reach instead of hitting them. A lock is an invitation.

Playstyle.AvoidConsumables: I don't like to use consumables
Playstyle.AvoidConsumablesHint: Potions, scrolls, bombs and the like get used far less, unless the moment demands it: a friend (or this character) close to death, or, with a helping playstyle, a friend in a bad way.
Playstyle.AvoidCostlySpells: I don't like to use spells that cost something
Playstyle.AvoidCostlySpellsHint: Spells that spend a slot, focus or a daily use get cast far less (cantrips are free), unless the moment demands it: a friend (or this character) close to death, or, with a helping playstyle, a friend in a bad way.

vengeful.Name: Vengeful
vengeful.Hint: Never forgets: hits back twice as hard, avenges fallen friends, and its grudges never cool.

relentless.Name: Relentless
relentless.Hint: Single-minded: sticks with the foe it's on, shrugs off setbacks, and keeps at a locked door.

lazy.Name: Lazy
lazy.Hint: As little as it can get away with: whatever foe is nearest (and not one worth a long walk), saves its resources, isn't much help to anyone, gives up fast, barely bothers with a locked door, and can't be bothered to hold a grudge.

Tracker.OpenHint: Estimate how this encounter will go
Tracker.NeedTwo: Add at least two tokens to the encounter to plan the battle.

Story.Title: The battle at {scene}
Story.Speaker: The Chronicle
Story.TablesMenuHint: Install the story's sentences as editable RollTables in this world.
Story.TablesHint: Every sentence of the Roleplay story is rolled from a table: an action table (delivery, damage type and how well it went, e.g. Melee · Slashing · Minor Success) plus a relationship table (e.g. Relationship · Enemy Leader · Failure). Install them to edit, add entries or translate; your world tables always win over the built-in ones.
Story.TablesInstalled: story tables installed in this world
Story.TablesLocale: Translators: a module can ship story/<language>.json with the same table keys; it is used automatically for that language.
Story.ReinstallConfirm: Replace every installed story table with the built-in version? Your edits to them will be lost.

Helper.Title: FastFighting needs a helper module for {system}
Helper.generic: No helper for {system}: using the experimental generic adapter. Results will be rough. See {list} for supported systems.
Helper.disabled: {module} is installed but not enabled in this world. Enable it in Manage Modules.
Helper.unknown: There is no FastFighting helper for {system} yet, so FastFighting is inactive in this world. Supported systems are listed at {list}.

Aftermath.tell: Tend the fallen and tell it

Concession.Luck: Luck check: {luck} on a d100 (needed {needed} or less).
Concession.Undone: Undone: it's back with its owner.
Concession.TheftLuck: Luck check: {luck} on a d100 (the thief needed {needed} or less).

Desire.Label: Desires
Desire.Hint: What this character wants, at whom, and how badly. Its tactics work out desires of their own each turn (the foe it would go for, a friend to heal); these come on top. The strongest leads, much weaker ones don't cross its mind, and a desire fades when it's thwarted (a locked door, a target out of reach, getting hurt on the way).
